One of Apple's proposals (or at least a mitigation measure) in response to the memory shortage is to source RAM from two Chinese companies, CXMT and YMTC.

Although doing so is not technically prohibited, it would put Apple at odds with the US government, and the idea now looks even less feasible due to two new developments…

As early as June, we learned that Apple was seeking approval from the Trump administration to source memory chips from China. Although there is no clear legal ban preventing companies from doing so, the Pentagon's blacklist means that if Apple were to use chips from these two companies, iPhones used by some or all federal employees could be banned. In addition, this would expose the Cupertino company to the risk of paying a high political or public relations price.

We pointed out at the time that Apple seemed unlikely to get approval, and now the latest report seems to put a few more nails in the coffin of this plan.

First, although sourcing from these two Chinese companies is not illegal at present, the New York Times reported that this situation may soon change.

Second, even if the situation remains unchanged, the Wall Street Journal reported that CXMT simply cannot meet Apple's order requirements.

I previously described this as an unlikely plan; now I would say it is extremely unlikely.
